page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by dedicated Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon clocked at 3.4 GHz, providing 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 128 GB RAM (4 GB per vCPU), supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. Storage is bundled locally with a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory and multi-threaded throughput. Memory bandwidth benchmarks place the system in the top tier, delivering 448.6 GB/sec read and 188.32 GB/sec write on large uncached blocks, complemented by top-tier PassMark database operation scores. Multi-threaded computational performance is strong, registering 66,288.64 in stress-ng and 20,037 in Geekbench multi-core. Conversely, single-core processing metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench fall within the median range, and large-parameter language model inference demonstrates weak throughput due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators or discrete hardware accelerators.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, coupled with dedicated ARM physical cores and high-speed local NVMe storage, makes the D32pds_v6 a cost-efficient platform for resource-dense horizontal workloads. It delivers high throughput efficiency per core for database operations, high-concurrency static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and transactional backend systems.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the ARM64 architecture and powered by 32 dedicated Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores clocked at 3.4 GHz. Featuring a standard 1:4 resource profile, the instance provides 128 GB of RAM, a 128 MB L3 cache, and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reveal top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 448 GB/sec on large block reads alongside top-tier database transaction processing. Multi-core compute performance is strong in stress-ng and Geekbench, though single-thread metrics remain in the middle tier. With dedicated single-threaded execution cores and fast local storage, the instance is well suited for transactional databases, CI/CD compilation workloads, high-throughput static web serving, and containerized microservice architectures requiring consistent execution and high memory throughput.
